cards.title: Move around in 3D
lines: Orbit: right-drag or move two fingers on a trackpad.
Pan: middle-drag or Shift + two fingers.
Zoom: mouse wheel or pinch.

cards.title: Create simple shapes
lines: Open Create to add a box, cylinder, sphere or another simple shape. You can also create a sketch here.

cards.title: Edit properties
lines: This panel lists your objects and their operations. Select an entry to see its properties.
Change dimensions, color and transformations here. You can also use the handles directly in the 3D view.

cards.title: Modify your model
lines: Use Modify to chamfer or round edges, extrude a face, revolve a profile or hollow out a solid.
Choose a tool and follow its selection instructions. Each change becomes an editable operation in the panel.

cards.title: Import and export
lines: Import kerCAD projects, STEP solids, SVG drawings, STL/OBJ reference meshes or JPG/PNG reference images.
Export your editable project as .kercad, or your model as STEP or STL for sharing and 3D printing.

cards.title: Explain with annotations
lines: Add text, dimensions, angles and circles to explain your design without changing its geometry.
Annotations are especially useful for teachers: highlight details, give feedback and correct students’ exercises directly on the model.

dashboardCards.title: Change your language and theme
lines: You can always return to this button to change the interface language and switch between the light and dark themes.
Your preferences are remembered in this browser.

dashboardCards.title: Your projects
lines: Projects is the main area of kerCAD, where you create and organize your designs.
Use the new-project card to start designing. You can return to Projects from the navigation at any time.

dashboardCards.title: Learn and teach with challenges
lines: Challenges are step-by-step tutorials for learning and teaching how to use kerCAD and design parts.
Open Challenges to explore the installed activities, import a challenge or create your own.

dashboardCards.title: Keep learning
lines: Open Documentation to learn more about kerCAD, explore its tools and deepen your design skills.
You can relaunch this introduction from the Information button whenever you need it.

sketchCards.title: Draw your sketch
lines: Use Draw to create lines, curves, rectangles, circles, slots and polygons.
Buttons with a corner triangle open a group of tools. Close a contour to use it in a 3D operation.

sketchCards.title: Add constraints
lines: Select points or edges, then use this panel to apply constraints or dimensions.
Horizontal, vertical, tangent and other relations preserve your design intent while you edit.

sketchCards.title: Edit your paths
lines: Use Edit to add or connect nodes, merge endpoints, trim geometry or smooth a path.
Select the geometry you want to change before choosing the tool.

sketchCards.title: Import an SVG
lines: Import an SVG drawing from your computer to bring vector paths into this sketch.
You can then edit the imported geometry and add constraints.

sketchCards.title: Explain with annotations
lines: Add text, dimensions, angles and circles without creating sketch geometry.
These annotations are useful for teachers and exercise corrections. They stay in the sketch and do not appear in the 3D view.

sketchCards.title: Keep the view clear
lines: These three buttons independently show or hide length labels, annotations and constraint labels.
Hide what you do not need while drawing. Your visibility preferences are remembered.

about.heroDescription: An approachable parametric CAD tool for students, teachers and curious minds. Turn an idea into a model, understand every step, and make it your own.
about.heroNote: In your browser. No account. No installation.
about.modelAlt: Illustration of a blue mechanical bracket with holes, a sketch and dimension guides
about.historyDescription: Go back. Change a dimension. Keep creating.
about.learningDescription: Less time finding your way around software. More time exploring shapes, making decisions and understanding how things are built.
about.studentDescription: Start with a shape or sketch. Move a handle, try a new dimension and see what changes. A visible operation history helps you understand the result—not just get there.
studentPoints: Work with real dimensions and constraints
about.teacherDescription: Build exercises in the integrated challenge editor. Add instructions, images and reference values, then share a single package with your class.
teacherPoints: Let students progress at their own pace
Annotate designs to explain and give feedback
about.sketchAlt: Illustrated constrained sketch of a rounded plate with holes and dimension annotations
about.sketchCaption: From an idea on a plane to a model you understand.
about.featureEyebrow: Simple to approach. Room to grow.
about.featureDescription: Start simple, then reach for the next tool when your project needs it.

featureGroups.title: Shape & transform
featureGroups.heading: Build. Adjust. Rebuild.
featureGroups.description: Combine basic shapes with editable operations. Position and rotation triads, parameter handles and numeric fields keep you in control.

featureGroups.title: Sketch & constrain
featureGroups.heading: Make your intent visible.
featureGroups.description: Draw profiles with lines, arcs, curves and shapes. Dimensions and geometric constraints help them keep the relationships you intend.
items: Lines, arcs, Bézier curves and freehand
featureGroups.alt: Illustrated 2D sketch with constraints and dimensions

featureGroups.title: Measure & explain
featureGroups.heading: A design that tells its story.
featureGroups.description: Use annotations to explain a part, highlight a detail or review an exercise. They are visual aids, not solid geometry.
featureGroups.alt: Illustration of a dimensioned part with visual feedback annotations

featureGroups.title: Organize & share
featureGroups.heading: Your work. Your next step.
featureGroups.description: Keep projects in your browser, exchange editable files and bring your models into other workflows. Export a backup to keep your work outside browser storage.
featureGroups.alt: Illustrated key tag design ready to share

about.challengeDescription: A challenge is a tutorial or exercise that lives beside the 3D workspace. Students can read a step, inspect its image and keep designing without leaving their project.

challengeSteps.title: Create the activity
challengeSteps.description: Set a title, author and cover. Add steps with text, images and as many reference parameters as you need.

challengeSteps.title: Capture what matters
challengeSteps.description: Frame a view of your model or upload an image. Arrange the steps in the order that suits your lesson.

challengeSteps.title: Share one ZIP
challengeSteps.description: Distribute the package through your classroom platform. Students import it and follow the steps at their own pace.

about.challengeName: A key tag, made by you
about.challengeInstruction: Add a cylinder and use it to make a hole. Leave enough material around the edge.
about.challengeCaption: Illustrated challenge example. Instructions stay beside the design.
about.privacyEyebrow: A workspace that fits your classroom
about.privacyDescription: kerCAD runs online without requiring an account. Projects are stored locally in the browser; export .kercad copies for backup or sharing. Schools can also run their own server and manage how they make the tool available.
privacyPoints: A private server for your school
about.communityDescription: kerCAD is already being used at IES Reino Aftasí. We would love to hear how other schools and organizations bring it into their work.
about.joinDescription: Are you using kerCAD in your classroom or organization? This space will grow with the people who make it part of their learning.
about.storiesDescription: Soon: real classroom experiences, student projects and ideas from teachers. For now, we are leaving room for the stories still taking shape.
about.finalTitle: One idea is all it takes.
about.finalDescription: Open a project, try a shape and see where it leads.
about.footer: Open-source 3D design for learning by doing.
about.credit: Designed with love by Pablo Gil Fernández

sections.title: Getting started
sections.content: Create an empty project, add shapes and adjust their parameters. Use the operation tree to revisit and edit each step.

sections.title: Sketches and constraints
sections.content: Draw lines and curves, add dimensions and constraints, and save the sketch to use it in 3D operations.
